thread:
sam: quick q — PR https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4023 touches `infra/` and `docs/` (small wording fix). CODEOWNERS has @infra-team for infra/ and @docs-team for docs/. GitHub is blocking merge with `required review from CODEOWNERS`. Who can approve this so we can merge? cc @kevin

marta: short answer: a CODEOWNER for the changed paths needs to approve. GitHub enforces that check server-side if the branch protection rule is on. Admins can bypass/merge, but we avoid that unless necessary.

kevin: if the PR modifies both paths, you'll need approvals covering both sets of owners. Approving only infra/ files won't satisfy docs/ ownership. Splitting is usually the fastest.

sam: ok — is there a documented override flow? sometimes a repo admin can merge with a label?

marta: we do have an ad-hoc override pattern but it requires a repo admin signoff. Options: 1) get a docs owner to approve, 2) split the PR into infra + docs, 3) ask @platform-admins (repo admins) to merge with an explicit override (they'll ask for context). We try option 1 or 2 first.

sam: noted. I'll ping docs owners. If we need the override, who's the right ping? alex?

kevin: alex or tanya from platform-admins. But again admins will want a short rationale in the PR and confirmation CI passed.

devops-bot: CI: check/circleci — all checks passed ✅

sam: thinking long-term — should we add @eng-platform to CODEOWNERS for `infra/` so product infra changes don't block? I can send a follow-up PR to update CODEOWNERS. Example snippet:
```
# CODEOWNERS (proposal)
/docs/ @docs-team
/infra/ @infra-team @eng-platform
```
Would that be acceptable?

marta: adding eng-platform to infra/ is fine as long as the team explicitly wants that responsibility. That change won't help the current PR (CODEOWNERS file is only consulted after merge), but it will reduce future friction. Please open a separate PR and tag both infra and eng-platform for review.

kevin: alternative for this PR: if the docs change is literally one-line typo, ask a docs owner for a quick approve — usually fast. If it's bulk edits, splitting feels cleaner. I'll take a look at the infra changes in ~30m and can approve that side once I review.

sam: thanks. I'll ping @docs-team in #documentation and split if they don't respond in 1h. Will post updates here.

marta: perfect. and if you end up needing admin override, @alex/tanya prefer a comment like: "Admin-override requested: PR 4023 — change summary + CI passed + reason why docs owner can't review". Keep it brief.

sam: got it — updating now.

kevin: FYI — if you split the PR, remember to rebase and keep commit messages small, that'll help the codeowners check run cleanly.

sam: thanks all :thumbsup:
